material_definitions:
A systematic study of Li(1+x)M(x)Ti(2-x)(PO4)3 with M=Al, Cr and Fe and 0 
T x 
T 1 has been carried out.
The base compound is LiTi2(PO4)3, and the materials were studied using X-ray and neutron powder diffraction and impedance spectroscopy.
The addition of trivalent metals leads to the occupation of M1 and a new M2' site by lithium atoms, increasing delocalization.

The bulk and grain boundary ionic conductivity show thermally activated behavior and increase with substituent content up to x = 0.2
-0.3.
The samples are NASICON-type solid solutions Li1+xMxTi2-x(PO4)3, where M=Al, Cr, or Fe, derived from LiTi2(PO4)3.
Electrical conductivity was measured using complex impedance spectroscopy to distinguish bulk dc ({ho}b) and grain boundary ({ho}gb) contributions.
Maximum conductivity values were found for x=0.3 in Al and Fe substituted samples and x=0.2 in Cr samples.
Grain boundary conductivity is typically two to three orders of magnitude lower than bulk conductivity.
The variation of activation energy is mainly attributed to the displacement of Li+ ions to M2' sites upon substitution, increasing disorder and pre-exponential factor.
